en: Itivuttaka 23:
Ekakanipāta,
Third Chapter (Tatiyavagga)
The Discourse on Both Benefits:
This was said by the Blessed One, said by the Arahant; thus have I heard:
"Bhikkhus, one thing, when developed and cultivated, stands having attained both benefits."
Both the welfare pertaining to the present life and that pertaining to future lives.
What is that one thing?
Heedfulness regarding wholesome states.
“Monks, this one thing, when developed and cultivated, stands having attained both kinds of welfare:
that pertaining to the present life and that pertaining to the future life.
Thus the Blessed One spoke.
In this regard, it is said:
"The wise praise heedfulness in the performance of meritorious deeds;"
The wise person, being diligent, attains both goals:
that which pertains to the present life, and—
That which is beneficial for the future life—
the wise person, through the realization of that benefit, is called "a sage."
This matter too was spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
The third [sutta].
